headline: Himachal Pradesh dismisses senior civil judge for graft | Shimla News
content: SHIMLA: Himachal government, in perhaps the first such instance, dismissed a senior civil judge from Himachal Pradesh Judicial Services after he was indicted for corruption in an inquiry by the High Court of Himachal Pradesh. In February 2007, Gaurav Sharma, a resident of Amritsar in Punjab, then posted as additional chief judicial magistrate of Sundernagar in Mandi district, was arrested by the team of officials from state vigilance and anti-corruption bureau and placed under suspension. A case of dishonouring of cheques had come up before Sharma when he was posted in Sundernagar. To settle matter Gaurav Sharma, then additional chief judicial magistrate of Sundernagar in Mandi district, had sought Rs 40,000 from a businessman who was struggling to get his money after cheque bounce to settle the matter. Graft charges proved in high court probe The businessman who was struggling to get his money after the cheque bounce was reportedly called by Sharma in his chamber to settle the matter and he (then judge) sought Rs 40,000 for it. A complaint was lodged with the state vigilance and anti-corruption department after which the vigilance team laid a trap and arrested Sharma when he was accepting the money at his residence. A case under Section 7 and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act was registered against him. Principal secretary (home) Rajneesh, in a notification issued on November 25, stated that the High Court of Himachal Pradesh had proposed to hold an inquiry against Gaurav Sharma, civil judge-cum-ACJM (under suspension) under Rule 14 of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 and the inquiry was conducted by the high court. He said when all the charges were proved in the inquiry, the High Court decided to recommend that the punishment of dismissal from service be imposed upon Sharma. The notification also mentioned said that the governor, Himachal Pradesh, having considered the recommendations of the high court and in exercise of the powers vested in him under Clause (ix) of Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, ordered the dismissal of Sharma from the Himachal Pradesh Judicial Services with immediate effect.
